beats.intro: Module fifteen. [[sub]]How to judge the credit of governments and public issuers.
beats.differ: Governments borrow differently from companies. [[use]]A company uses debt to build profits, and repays from operating cash flow. A government uses debt for fiscal policy and public services, and repays from taxes and other revenue. [[tax]]Its right to tax makes sovereign bonds the lowest credit risk in their own country. [[abil]]Analysts study both the ability to pay, and the willingness to pay. [[imm]]Willingness matters because of sovereign immunity. Bondholders cannot force a government into bankruptcy, or liquidate its assets. [[restr]]Instead, with help from lenders like the International Monetary Fund, debts are usually restructured. Uruguay extended its bond maturities by five years in two thousand three, and analysts judged it a default in substance.
beats.qual: Qualitative factors come first. [[inst]]Institutions and policy: rule of law, property rights, transparency, and political stability. [[fisc]]Fiscal flexibility: discipline in taxes and spending. In two thousand twenty one, Moody's improved its outlook on Romania, expecting sustained fiscal consolidation. [[mon]]Monetary effectiveness: a central bank independent of the treasury is less likely to print money to fund debt. [[eco]]Economic flexibility: large, diversified economies are stronger. Emerging economies often depend on one commodity. [[ext]]And external status: whether the currency is a reserve currency. Foreign investors will hold it, which expands borrowing power. Many emerging markets have capital controls, and rely on lenders like the International Monetary Fund.
beats.quant: Quantitative factors start with fiscal strength. [[burden]]Debt burden ratios, like debt to G D P, or debt to revenue, work like leverage. [[afford]]Debt affordability ratios, like interest to revenue, measure coverage. [[rule]]A higher burden, or lower affordability, means lower credit quality. [[growth]]Then growth and stability: the size of the economy, income per person, and how steady real growth is. [[euro]]In the European debt crisis, high debt to G D P, plus rising deficits, pushed borrowing spreads over Germany sharply wider.
beats.nonsov: Other public issuers have their own analysis. [[agency]]Agencies are quasi-government entities with a public mission. Investors assume government support, and the rating often equals the sovereign's. An airport authority owned by Hong Kong, for example, was rated like its government. [[dev]]Development banks and similar bodies may have an explicit government guarantee. [[reg]]Regional and local governments have their own taxes and revenues, but their credit quality can differ from the sovereign's. [[go]]General obligation bonds are backed by the issuer's general taxing power, and are analyzed like sovereign debt. [[rev]]Revenue bonds are backed by the cash flows of a specific project, and are analyzed like a corporate project.
beats.wrap: Let's recap. [[w1]]Sovereigns repay from taxes, but willingness to pay matters too. [[w2]]Qualitative factors: institutions, fiscal, monetary, economic, and external. [[w3]]Quantitative factors: debt burden, affordability, growth, and stability. [[w4]]Agencies track the sovereign. Local debt is general obligation or revenue bonds.
